Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:89: Further, purity is found regarding the heart: (Psalms 51:12), "a pure heart God has created for me" — and this is the essential point directed at our exposition regarding clinging: that if the heart is pure, all the limbs are pure, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained in Midrash Shocher Tov (Midrash Tehillim, mizmor 14), in these words: "I, the Lord, search the heart, I test the kidneys" (Jeremiah 17:10) — why does He mention the heart and the kidneys more than all the other limbs? Rather, the eyes follow the heart, and the 248 limbs follow the heart, and since the kidneys give counsel and the heart concludes, therefore He mentions only these — and the Holy One, blessed be He, tests them. And so it says (I Chronicles 28:9), "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him, for the Lord searches all hearts" — these are the two hearts, the good inclination and the evil inclination. A parable of an architect who built the province's chambers, drains, and caves; after some time he became a tax-collector, and the people of the province would hide from him within the chambers and within the caves; he said to them, fools, why do you hide? Did I not build this province? Did I not build the caves and the chambers? So too (Isaiah 29:15), "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the Lord." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:90: In the Gate of Fear, chapter 7, we quoted a parable close to this one; however, that parable was said regarding one who commits a transgression in secret, while here it is expounded regarding one who thinks thoughts in his heart, as it says, "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the Lord" — and the chambers and caves mentioned in the passage are the chambers of the heart and kidneys.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:91: When a person contemplates this matter, he will purify his thought — for the Name created him, and created his heart and his kidneys, and knows his secrets, and before Him all is revealed, darkness as light, and he always stands before Him — how then could he not be ashamed to think a thing against His will?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:92: So too our sages, of blessed memory, further explained in Bereishit Rabbah on the verse (Jeremiah 32:19), "great in counsel," etc., in these words: "great" — "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm; nothing is too wonderful for You" (ibid. 32:17). Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah: what is meant by "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth"? From that hour, nothing has been too wonderful for You. Rabbi Chaggai said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak (I Chronicles 28:9), "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the Lord searches all hearts and understands every inclination of the thoughts" — before the thought is completed in a person's heart, it is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: before a creature is formed, his thought is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan applied this to himself (Psalms 139:4), "for there is not a word on my tongue, but, behold, O Lord, You know it entirely" — before my tongue is betrothed [to speech], behold, O Lord, You know it entirely. — end of quotation. Here, from the plain sense of these words there is proof for our intent, without needing to further scrutinize it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:93: When a person contemplates that the Shechinah is above his head, it is fitting that he purify his brain and his heart, so that the Shechinah find a place to rest — for these are the two chief organs of man, in which the essence of vitality resides, and therefore they must be purified from every blemish that damages them, for a slight matter will blemish them due to their great fineness and spirituality, for they allude to a supernal place in Atzilut, as explained in the Tikkunim (Introduction, 17a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:94: Corresponding to the purity of thought, David the king, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart." I have already explained above "clean hands," and quoted the words of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, regarding cleanliness. And it says afterward, "and a pure heart" — in this manner, that he does not draw his will and his heart to another side, but rather draws them after the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. "Who has not lifted his soul in vain" — "his soul" is written but "my soul" is read; and they have established that "my soul" is the soul of David, the aspect of faithfulness, and "his soul" is literally the soul of a person — for when his soul departs from this world, it ascends through the fitting deeds of the world it was sustained by, to go among all those [souls], as in (Psalms 116:9), "I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living" — and because "he has not lifted his soul in vain, he shall receive a blessing from the Lord," etc. — end of quotation. Here it is explained in this passage the greatness of one who rectifies his deeds and thoughts for the service of his Creator — because his soul is a part of the Shechinah, this being "his soul" and "my soul," all one — and according to the rectification of his soul, so he rectifies above; therefore he shall merit what David the king, peace be upon him, said, "I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living," and "shall receive a blessing from the Lord" — namely, the Shechinah, as is known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:95: From the affirmative you understand the negative: that whoever lifts his soul in vain and defiles his thought damages, Heaven forbid, above, and his soul shall not ascend above to the mountain of the Lord nor to His holy place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:96: Now, one must purify the heart from jealousy, hatred, rivalry, and from all the evil traits that depend on the heart, such as worry, sighing, sadness, anger, mockery, and the like; and when the heart is free of all this it is a fine dwelling for the Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, 22b), that a person must rectify a fine dwelling for the Shechinah in his heart — namely, through the rectification explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:97: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 29, end of p. 72) that one's inside must be like his outside; it says there that the wine is the Torah, and it must be guarded and sealed in a good jug, and the jug is the heart; and if this jug has become tainted with the wine of the evil inclination, it needs rinsing three times, and needs rinsing and washing like a cup of blessing — namely, that his inside be like his outside — and this in these words: and when this jug, which is the heart, is pure inside and out, wisdom dwells there, of which it is said (Proverbs 8:22), "the Lord acquired [kanani] me as the beginning of His way" — "kanani" is surely a jug [kankan]; and if this jug is pure, of it is said, "and he shall be clean [ve-nikkah]," and if not, "he who touches it shall not be clean" (ibid. 6:29). — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:98: So too the matter of purity of thought — for the brain is a more important and finer vessel than the heart, and therefore it is in the head; and you know regarding tefillin that one does not lower from a greater holiness to a lesser holiness, namely, [taking] the strap of the head [tefillah] to make it into that of the hand — and although the passages written for the head are the same as those for the hand, nevertheless, since they were placed on the head, they acquired a higher rank and spirituality, and one should not lower them to make them into that of the hand. Therefore one must purify his thought all the more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:99: Whoever merits to purify his thought shall merit in the future what our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 17a): the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads. And they merit the crown upon the head only because they purified the brain in their heads, so that the Shechinah be crowned upon them — and in the future too they merit this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:100: It appears that the secret of "their crowns upon their heads" is what is said regarding Joshua the High Priest (Zechariah 3:5), "and they placed the pure turban upon his head" — and it says "pure turban" because the crown was made for him only because he purified his thought, as explained. It may also be said, and this seems to be the essential meaning, that the pure turban was made for him from the commandments that depend on the head, such as donning tefillin, and the spreading of tzitzit upon his head, and the commandment of the corners of the head [pe'ot]; and likewise purity of thought through the pure intentions by which a person unifies himself with his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:101: Regarding purity, there are found in the Zohar and Ra'aya Meheimna places that differ from one another. In parashat Korach (176a), and likewise in parashat Chukat (180b), it is explained that a priest is "holy" and a Levite is "pure," and therefore the Red Heifer, which is from the left side, came to purify and not to sanctify, for the essence of purity is on the left. But in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Ekev 273b), purity is on the right and holiness on the left.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:102: Regarding holiness, it will be explained further on, with God's help. However, regarding purity, it seems to me that there are two kinds of purity: the first is purity through water, as explained above, and water is known to be from the side of Chesed. And there is purity from the left side, as it is written (Numbers 31:23), "everything that can withstand fire, you shall pass through fire, and it shall be pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:103: Likewise, vessels are purified in two ways: through water — namely, immersion for eating vessels that did not go through fire — or purification through fire if they were used with fire, as Scripture says, "everything that can withstand fire, you shall pass through fire, and it shall be pure," etc., "whatever cannot withstand fire, you shall pass through water."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:104: Likewise regarding the purification of souls from their blemish, purification must correspond to the blemish — this being the four categories of atonement that Rabbi Yishmael would expound (Yoma 86a): if a person transgressed a positive commandment and repented, he is forgiven immediately, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:22), "return, backsliding children, I will heal your backslidings." This category of atonement is from the side of Chesed, for it is known (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 107b) that the 248 positive commandments are from the right side and the negative commandments from the left side; therefore the blemish of a positive commandment, being in Chesed, once he repents, is forgiven immediately — this being purification from the side of the waters of Chesed, which purify him, and he is forgiven immediately.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:105: Transgressing a positive commandment means that he was lazy in fulfilling the commandments, such as [not eating] matzah on Passover, and the like — namely, the nullification of the commandment through simply sitting and not acting. Its rectification is alacrity from then on to fulfill what is within his power, and the waters — namely, the waters of supernal atonement — are poured forth and wash away that blemish in the soul, for even the nullification of a commandment causes a blemish in the soul, though not as severe as transgressing a negative commandment; and purification in the mikveh waters will avail to purify what was neglected in the commandment. The reason is that when a person fulfills the commandment, he draws supernal light to clothe his soul, and in his nullification of the commandment, immediately the outside force presents itself there and rests upon him, for they are called "these" [eleh] and rest wherever is empty of holiness, as explained in the Zohar, parashat Terumah (128a), that they rest upon man freely — and especially when he is idle, "like finds like" and is stirred up. Therefore, in order to strip off from himself that spirit of impurity, purification is needed in the mikveh waters, which are from the side of Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:106: When the blemish is in a negative commandment — namely, the second category of atonement — if a person transgressed a negative commandment and repents, repentance suspends [the punishment] and Yom Kippur atones, as it is said (Leviticus 16:30), "for on this day He shall atone for you, to purify you." If a person transgressed [a sin punishable by] excision [karet] or death by the court, and repents, repentance and Yom Kippur suspend and afflictions scour away [the sin], as it is said (Psalms 89:33), "then I will punish their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues." But one who is guilty of desecrating the Divine Name, etc. [death alone atones]. Now, these three categories are all included under negative commandments, and therefore purification for all of them is through the fire of Gevurah — for the fast of Yom Kippur purifies through the affliction of one's soul and the offering of his fat and blood, melted by the fire of affliction, as will be further explained regarding fasting, that fasting is a purifying fire for the fire of the inclination, in the manner of "everything that can withstand fire"; and likewise afflictions and plagues are all surely purification from the side of fire, and there is no need to mention the day of death. Therefore it is the nature of fire to refine both within and without — in the manner that the blemish, that he heated himself up with the fire of the inclination, so too the purification and refining must be [through fire]; and therefore the essence of purification is through fire, in the manner of (Pesachim 2:1), "the removal of chametz is only through burning" — and therefore fasting is efficacious for a penitent to purify and refine him within and without, and so too wearing sackcloth on his flesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:107: The Torah is found to contain both these purifications, and therefore our sages, of blessed memory, explained that Torah is likened to fire, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:29), "is not My word like fire"; and it is likened to water, as it is said (Isaiah 55:1), "ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters." The reason is that the Torah is the secret of the central line, and it is fitting that everything be included within it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:108: All the particular aspects explained are all found in the Torah — whether to strip off the spirit of impurity, whether to cool the impurity from the fire of the inclination, whether to refine the inclination — and therefore it is written of it (Psalms 12:7), "the words of the Lord are pure words."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:109: So too the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (parashat Kedoshim 80b) that the essence of purification is through Torah, in these words: come and see, a person is never purified except through words of Torah; therefore words of Torah do not receive impurity, because it stands to purify these impure ones, and healing is found in the Torah, as it is written (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing for your navel and marrow for your bones," and it is written (ibid. 10:27), "the fear of the Lord adds days." Purification is found in Torah, as it is written (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever" — what is "enduring forever"? That it stands constantly in that purity and never departs from it. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:110: The essence of purification of thought is through engaging in Torah, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 30b): I created the evil inclination, I created for it a remedy [i.e., the Torah]. And Maimonides wrote at the end of the Laws of Forbidden Relations, in these words: beyond all this, they said, one should divert himself and his thought to words of Torah and broaden his mind in wisdom, for thoughts of forbidden relations grow strong only in a heart empty of wisdom, and regarding wisdom it says (Proverbs 5:19), "a loving hind and a graceful doe," etc. Therefore we placed the purification of Torah last in the matter of purity, because it surpasses all and is the essence of all purifications: "purity leads to holiness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:111: The Ra'avad explained in the Gate of Holiness the matter of "purity leads to holiness," and he began the Gate with the verse (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy," and said, regarding our subject, in these words: I shall first explain what the two holinesses mentioned in this verse are. Likewise, what is said in the baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, "purity leads to holiness" — I shall explain what purity is and what holiness is, and from this you will know what the two holinesses are.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:112: I say first, that impurities are of two kinds: those found through physical contact, and those not through contact. Through contact — such as touching carcasses and carrying them, touching creeping things, and the beds and seats of a zav, a zavah, and a metzora, and seeing a nocturnal emission, and the impurity of a corpse. Likewise one who commits transgressions, such as one who engages in forbidden sexual relations, and one who eats forbidden things — these are the impurities that are through contact, for one who engages in forbidden sexual relations and eats forbidden things is called impure, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 18:24), "do not defile yourselves with any of these," and "and you shall become impure through them" (Leviticus 11:43). And the impurity that is not through contact — such as seeing with the eyes, hearing with the ears, and utterance of the lips, regarding something not fitting to see, hear, or speak of, and the heart's contemplation of forbidden matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:113: Purity too is found through contact and not through contact. The purification of contacts, carrying, nocturnal emission, plagues, and the impurity of a corpse is through immersions and sprinklings, and the other matters explained regarding the metzora — this is the purity of contact. And the purity that is not through contact is abstaining from transgression and forbidden things, cleanliness of heart, thought, and tongue, and the closing of the eyes and the sealing of the ears from seeing and hearing evil — all these are called "pure," as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "from all your sins before the Lord you shall be purified," and it is written (Ezekiel 36:25), "from all your impurities and from all your idols I will purify you," and it is written (Isaiah 33:15), "and shuts his eyes from seeing evil," etc., and it is written (Proverbs 22:11), "he who loves purity of heart, whose lips are gracious, the king is his friend," and it is written (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart" — and if one is careful about these, he is called pure, and one who is not careful is called impure; and one who speaks things not fitting for him is called "impure of lips," and one who is careful about this is called "pure of lips."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:114: It follows that impurity is of two kinds and purity of two kinds, except that there is a superiority between abstaining from the impurity of transgressions and forbidden things and abstaining from other impurities — for one who abstains from contacts and other similar impurities is called only "pure," as it is written (Leviticus 14:8), "and he shall wash in water and be pure." But one who abstains from transgressions and forbidden things is called both "pure" and "holy" — pure, as we said, and holy, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy," and in the passage of creeping things it is likewise written (Leviticus 11:44), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy." Moreover, the other impurities do not involve the impurity of thought, but regarding the impurity of transgressions and forbidden things, just as one must abstain from the physical acts of the transgression, so one must abstain from thinking of them, so that he not contemplate the transgression in his heart; and if a thought of them comes to him, he must force himself to remove it from his heart — how much more so that he not intend to complete it in his heart. And since a completed thought is what leads to action, and is considered as an action, of this it is said (Ezekiel 14:5), "in order to grasp the house of Israel by their heart" — and this is the second holiness that Scripture warns of: "and you shall sanctify yourselves" through action, "and be holy" through thought. Do you not see what is written at the end of the verse, "for I am holy" — just as I am holy in action and in thought, so you shall be holy — from this you learn that a person is not called holy until he sanctifies himself in action and in thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:115: Now you shall understand and know that a person cannot attain this attribute until he sets aside, of what is permitted to him, some portion of it, and fences himself in with a fence of permitted things that are the way and path toward habituating oneself to transgression — in the manner they said (Niddah 13b), whoever puts his hand below his navel, let his hand be cut off; and as they said (ibid.), whoever holds his member and urinates is as though he brings a flood upon the world; and as Rabbi Yosi said (Shabbat 118b), I have never gazed at my own circumcised member — and they asked, if so, why do they call him "our holy Rabbi"? They answered him, Rabbi, he had an extra measure of piety, in that he never put his hand beneath his belt. All this abstinence was a fence, so that the desire for forbidden relations would not attach itself to him — for the inclination quarrels with man and accuses him, to seduce and incite him, and this is its way: it seduces him to satisfy his soul and fulfill all his desires with everything permitted to him, and after it has taught him to fulfill all his desires with the hunger of his soul, when he cannot find what he wants in what is permitted to him, it will incite him to fulfill his desires easily with what is forbidden, and from the light [prohibition] to the severe, and from the severe to something more severe still, until it tells him, go worship idols and deny Him who spoke and the world came to be — that there is no judgment, no Judge, no Gan Eden, no Gehinnom, and no other world. So too the sage said in the Book of Ecclesiastes (see Ecclesiastes 9:3), "this is an evil thing among all that is done under the sun," etc., "for the living know that they shall die," etc., "go, eat your bread with joy," etc., "see life with the wife whom you love," etc. — all these are words of the evil inclination. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:116: We shall not elaborate on the explanation of Scripture as he, of blessed memory, explained it, so as not to lengthen this. He says afterward: and therefore one must strengthen and empower himself and stand firm over his own soul to fight against his desires, so that he have an advantage in his soul over the soul of an animal, which has no restraint over anything it wishes to attain of its desire — for the desire that overpowers a person is from the power of the vegetative soul, which is the animal soul; and therefore the wicked, who follow after their desires, are compared to animals, as Scripture says (see Psalms 49:13), "man in his glory does not endure," etc., and the sage said (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the animal goes downward to the earth" — "the spirit of man" means the soul of the righteous, which ascends upward, and "the spirit of the animal that goes downward" means the soul of the wicked, who are compared to animals.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:117: The matter is thus: he said above this (v. 20), "all go to one place; all were from the dust and all shall return to the dust," etc. — that is, there is no distinction in death between the righteous and the wicked, nor even between man and animal, for all shall die and return to the dust, and among all the living none can distinguish any superiority between one and the other; and who knows regarding the superiority of souls, whether the soul of a righteous man ascends upward or the soul of a wicked man descends downward to the earth — that is, below the earth, which is the deep Sheol — none among all the living can recognize that superiority except the Creator alone. This matter is known through wisdom to the wise, the possessors of contemplation, but there is no evident proof of it regarding life and death, for in this all are equal; therefore it says, "who knows" — that is, who recognizes their superiority — for if the superiority were demonstrable, both the wise and the foolish would know it, but there is no sign or proof of it in life or death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:118: Now, although all souls are equal, in their death they return to the place of their desire and the effort of their lifetime — for the soul of the righteous, taken from the place of intellect, having held fast to its intellect and its desire, returns in death to the place of its origin, from where it came. But the soul of the wicked, which desired the vanities of the world and its pleasures, and did not remember its former origin, likewise returns to the place of its desire. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:119: At the conclusion of the Gate, he explained in brief the passage we are engaged in explaining, and he, of blessed memory, said: watchfulness [zehirut] is when a person is watchful and guards himself before the matter comes to his hand. Alacrity [zerizut] is at the time of the deed, that he perform his commandment with alacrity and not laziness, and if a sin comes to his hand, he should flee and separate from it with alacrity. Cleanliness [nekiyut] is the cleanliness of his body and garments from soiling, in the manner they said (Shabbat 114a), any Torah scholar found with a grease stain on his flesh is liable to death. Purity [taharah] comes from the totality of impurities, that he guard himself from impurities, and if he touches them, he should purify himself and eat his non-sacred food in purity. Holiness [kedushah] is the holiness of the heart and thought, as we have said. Piety [chasidut] is one who acts beyond the letter of the law in every matter, called a chasid — and all these he explains their reasons from Scripture at length; end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:120: According to our own method, let us return to explain the matter of "purity leads to holiness" and the rest of the passage; and although above we did not explain anything regarding abstinence [perishut], since we said it is included within holiness, nevertheless, according to the version of our text, it is fitting to explain something regarding it. The matter is that holiness includes two things, as we elaborated at length in the Gate of Holiness: the first is "turn from evil," and the second is "do good"; and according to our version we say that abstinence is the aspect of "turn from evil," and holiness is "do good." But according to the Yerushalmi, which does not include "perishut," both aspects are included within holiness, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:121: The intent of saying "purity leads to holiness" is that the essence of purity is the purification of each and every limb from blemish, such as purification of the tongue from slander and other damaging things, purification of the eyes from gazing upon nakedness, and similarly with the other limbs. But holiness is a further, more inward boundary — for beyond not speaking slander, he should increase silence, and the holiness of the eye, that he not gaze beyond four cubits, as we elaborated at length in the Gate of Holiness regarding the holiness of each and every limb.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:122: The Ra'avad, peace be upon him, explained in the Gate of Holiness the matter of "holiness leads to humility." The matter is that when a person reaches this holiness mentioned, humility necessarily follows from it, the reason being that the essence of holiness is a person's abstention from the affairs of the world, in order to cling to his Creator, as it says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy" — and we elaborated at length in the Gate of Holiness on the explanation of this verse; see there. And since a person clings to his Creator, humility necessarily follows upon him — for if he is insulted and disgraced, he will not consider this world important enough to respond to his insult, for what people say about him is a disgrace of this world, and all pertains only to the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:123: And even if they insult him regarding a matter touching the blemish of his soul, the soul, which is holy, does not pay attention to the disgrace done to it, for he considers this an atonement for his sin, and all is a cause from Him, blessed be He, to atone for his sin, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (II Samuel 16:10), "the Lord has said to him, curse." Further, if they disgrace it, its Master, to whom it clings, will watch over it — and so David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 38:15), "and I am like a man who does not hear, and in whose mouth there are no arguments; for I have hoped in You, O Lord; You will answer, O Lord my God" — and further, if a servant standing before his master, and someone comes and disgraces him before the king, it is a disgrace for the servant to respond before his master; and for these two reasons David the king, peace be upon him, said "for I have hoped in You, O Lord." And for the second reason, "for I have hoped in You, O Lord" is precise — like a servant sitting before his master, waiting for the master to respond to his insult; and for the first reason, one may examine the precision of "You will answer, O Lord my God" — since You are my God, that my soul clings to You, and You are my God, it is fitting for You to watch over its insult.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:124: It is also possible [to understand] the attribute of humility in the manner of Moses our teacher's humility, peace be upon him — for when Miriam and Aaron spoke about him, it is written there (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was very humble." And there is a hint in the Tikkunim (5b) as to the reason for his humility: because of his great clinging to the Creator, he was ashamed to separate from Him to respond, and the Name responded on his behalf. And by this manner too, one may say that David the king, peace be upon him, said, "You will answer, O Lord my God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:125: Also, the attribute of humility comes to a person through contemplating the greatness of the Former, which has no end or limit — as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?" — that we are not within the bounds of a created being compared to His greatness, exalted be He — as we shall elaborate further on this in the Gate of Humility, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:126: This is the inward fear explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2 — to fear His greatness. This fear is attained only through holiness, as it is written (Psalms 34:10), "fear the Lord, His holy ones" — for if one follows the desires of the world, he has no fear at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:127: It follows that all the grades mentioned that lead to holiness are themselves aspects of fear, and holiness is included among them, and fear is bound to humility. So too are the words of the Rashbi, peace be upon him (Tikkunei Zohar 5b): "and humility is bound to fear" — this is what is written (Proverbs 22:4), "the reward of humility is the fear of the Lord" — and we quoted this passage in the Gate of Fear, chapter 3.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:128: It follows that saying "holiness leads to humility" is the matter of "fear leads to humility," and this is when a person contemplates, when he is insulted and everything is said against him, that he is not important as a creature since he does not respond — for none responds except one who considers himself something and says, one such as me should be insulted [i.e., defends his honor]; but one who considers himself as not being a creature [of significance], in the manner of "and what are we" that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said, surely will not respond. Further, he should consider that what is said about him is true — that it is a diminishment in the being of the world's creation, because of his sins, such that it would have been better for him had he not been created — and he should not consider himself to hold the status of a [significant] creature, and should not come to respond at all.
